MIT

plugins.description: 把本机 WorkBuddy、Trae、Qoder 的桌面登录接入 DeepSeek Harness：每家一个 OpenAI 兼容的本地端点，账号池、自动换号与设置面板。
plugins.readme_text:
WTQ Pool

DeepSeek Harness 版 · PI-Desktop 版

把本机已登录的 WorkBuddy、Trae、Qoder 账号接入 DeepSeek Harness，限流或额度用尽时自动换号。

English | 简体中文

安装 · 使用 · 功能 · 设置 · 更新日志 · 问题反馈

把本机 WorkBuddy、Trae、Qoder 的桌面登录接入 DeepSeek Harness。WorkBuddy 被限流或额度用尽时自动换号；Trae、Qoder 按请求选择账号，认证失败、限流或余额耗尽时换下一个登录重试，模型不存在、请求体非法这类请求自身的问题则按上游原样应答。三个来源独立开关，国内与国际账号分别成组。 限流按上游给出的等待时间冷却，上游只在响应头给出时以它为准；额度用尽与登录失效不会自行恢复，该账号会退出轮换，直到余额重新读到或重新登录。上游主机不可达时换下一个登录重试。 ## 预览 设置面板界面如下（默认亮色）： ![账号池](https://github.com/chengzhi-c/dsh-wtq-pool/raw/main/docs/preview-pool.png) 面板载入时读取 DeepSeek Harness 的外观设置；宿主切换主题后须重新载入面板： ![暗色主题](https://github.com/chengzhi-c/dsh-wtq-pool/raw/main/docs/preview-dark.png) 模型页可以改显示名、上下文窗口、输出上限、思考等级和贴图。Trae 目录给出费率的模型会带上 `x0.79` 这样的费率标签，未给出费率的模型（以及 Qoder 全部模型）不标注： ![模型设置](https://github.com/chengzhi-c/dsh-wtq-pool/raw/main/docs/preview-models.png) 在线预览：。 `docs/index.html` 用虚构演示数据加载实际面板代码，支持来源切换、模型设置和主题预览，不读取本机账号或令牌。 ![预览页](https://github.com/chengzhi-c/dsh-wtq-pool/raw/main/docs/preview-page.png) 开启 `showComposerPoints` 后，输入框工具栏显示当前模型的账号积分，点击可查看该组账号并切换账号。下图由实际输入框扩展离屏渲染： ![输入框积分](https://github.com/chengzhi-c/dsh-wtq-pool/raw/main/docs/preview-composer.png) 本地预览需先克隆仓库，再运行 `node docs/serve.cjs` 并打开它输出的地址。该页面不能用 `file://` 打开，浏览器不允许它读取同目录的面板文件。 ## 功能 - 复用本机登录：只读三家桌面 App 已保存的登录文件，不发起自己的 OAuth，不额外要一次授权。 - 按 region 注册模型分组：三家各自的 region 各注册成一个 provider，可以同时开启；没有账号的 region 不注册。 - 账号分发：WorkBuddy 支持先用一个账号、轮流使用、临期积分优先和同一对话固定一个账号，并在限流或额度用尽时自动换号；Trae、Qoder 支持轮流使用与临期积分优先，认证失败、限流或余额耗尽时换下一个登录重试。 - 积分自动化：自动签到默认关闭。开启后的定时任务与「立即运行」执行同一轮，包含三家签到、WorkBuddy 国内账号的连登奖励、任务奖励和猫猫旅行。连登天数由上游按对话推进，该轮在每个国内账号读取连登档位前先补发一次对话活动上报，因此档位到点即可解锁领取，不需要用户自己进 WorkBuddy 聊一句。 - 输入框积分：开启 `showComposerPoints` 后，输入框工具栏显示当前模型使用的账号余额，点开可换号。功能关闭后浮层停止轮询。 - 面板：账号状态、池状态、模型勾选、连接检查都在插件页的「账号池」卡片里。模型目录启动时加载，缓存过期后按需刷新，空闲不轮询。停用的账号不参与探测，也不让面板一直显示「检测中」。 - 连接检查：每条发现都带判定。网关没在听、模型目录读不到、发布的地址与实际绑定的不一致、provider 没被宿主接受，都算失败并给出要改什么。网关启动失败时给出失败原因，面板按地址漂移提示重启。检查自己出错时也作为一条发现写进报告，而不是让整条通道失败。 ## 安装 本地包：在源码目录执行 `pnpm install && pnpm run build && npm pack --pack-destination dist`，再安装生成的 `.tgz`： ```powershell $package = (Get-ChildItem .\dist\*.tgz | Sort-Object LastWriteTime | Select-Object -Last 1).FullName dsh plugin --profile desktop add $package ``` 需要 DeepSeek Harness 0.2.0 线（`package.json` 的 `engines.dsh`：`>=0.2.0-rc.1 <0.2.1`）与 Node `^22.19.0 || >=24.0.0`。 使用实际 profile 名替换 `desktop`。若 `dsh` 不在 PATH，使用安装目录中的 CLI。也可按 npm 包名 `dsh-wtq-pool` 或仓库地址安装；按仓库地址安装时 pnpm 会执行 `prepare` 脚本从源码构建，需要在 profile 的 `pnpm-workspace.yaml` 里写 `allowBuilds: dsh-wtq-pool: true`，并钉在某个 commit 上。 **面板在哪儿**：在侧边栏进入 **插件**，点开 **dsh-wtq-pool** 那张卡片（或它旁边的 **配置**），完整面板嵌在卡片里。模型分组没出现时，按面板顶部的提示重启 dsh。 ## 使用 在各家桌面 App 中登录后，点击「重新检测账号」。WorkBuddy 支持读取多个已保存登录，5.6 起的 `$wbEncrypted` 登录通过本机 WorkBuddy 获取密钥。Trae 国内版有 Trae CN 与 TRAE SOLO CN 两个登录位；Qoder 每个安装仅保存一个登录，重新登录会覆盖前一个。 顶层选来源，下面三屏： - **账号池**：每个号的标签、剩余积分、额度到期时间、冷却状态、签到进度；可单独停用某个号、移除它，或指定某个 region 优先用哪个号。WorkBuddy 的分发有先用一个账号、轮流使用、临期积分优先、同一对话固定一个账号；Trae 与 Qoder 有轮流使用和临期积分优先。 - **模型**：勾选这个 region 要暴露的模型，未勾选的不进模型选择器。可改显示名、上下文窗口、输出上限、思考等级和贴图支持。一个模型组最多发布 64 个，超出的标「未发布」，网关仍会服务它们。 - **连接检查**：逐条报出网关在不在听、模型目录读到几个、注册的地址与实际绑定的是否一致、每个 provider 有没有被宿主接受，并可复制整份报告。网关启动失败时给出失败原因，面板按地址漂移提示重启。 签到可单账号执行，也可在标题栏一次领完该来源。自动签到默认关闭，开启后默认于 09:00（北京时间）执行；当天错过的时段在当天内的下一次启动仍会补领，跨天则不补。Trae 的每日签到每台设备限领一次，Qoder 的新一轮在每天 10:00（北京时间）开出。 ## 设置 这些键全部经宿主设置 schema 声明，改动写回 profile 后即生效： | 键 | 默认（生效值） | 说明 | | --- | --- | --- | | `enabled` | `true` | 关闭后网关不启动 | | `sourceWorkbuddy` / `sourceTrae` / `sourceQoder` | `true` | 关闭后该来源不扫描、不发布、不请求 | | `distribution` | `priority` | WorkBuddy 池的发放方式：`priority` 先用一个账号，`round-robin` 均摊，`expiry` 优先消耗临期积分，`sticky` 同一对话固定 | | `sourceDistributions` | `{}` | Trae、Qoder 的分发方式：`round-robin` / `expiry`；兼容旧值 `priority` | | `cooldownSeconds` | `60` | 限流冷却时长。上游报出重置时间时以它为准，按北京时间 | | `creditReserves` | `{}` | 按账号 id 设定的积分保底，余额低于它的账号不参与分发 | | `authFile` | `""` | WorkBuddy 登录文件路径；扫描其所在目录的全部 `.info` 登录，留空自动发现 | | `autoCheckin` | `{"enabled":false,"hours":[9]}` | 自动签到的开关与时点；`hours` 为北京时间整点，留空用 09:00 | | `showComposerPoints` | `false` | 在输入框工具栏显示当前账号积分 | | `disabledAccountIds` | `[]` | 面板里停用的账号 id | | `disabledRegions` | `[]` | 单独停用的 region，形如 `source:region` | | `modelSelection` | `{}` | 每个网关勾选哪些模型，以及显示名、上下文窗口等覆写 | | `preferredAccountIds` | `{}` | WorkBuddy 每个 region 的首选账号 | | `preferredSourceAccounts` | `{}` | Trae、Qoder 每个 region 的首选账号，键为 `source:region` | | `removedAccounts` | `[]` | 从池里移除的账号，标签与 region 一并保留，面板可据此提供恢复 | 默认列是生效值：`autoCheckin.hours` 存为空数组，运行时归一为 `[9]`；`authFile` 未设或留空即自动发现。 模型勾选和首选账号由面板保存。命令面板里也可打开面板、重新检测、清除冷却、全部签到、连接检查。 ## 端口 ``` WorkBuddy 42831 / 42841 Trae 42851 / 42861 Qoder 42871 / 42881 ``` 以上为首选端口。被占用时网关绑定临时端口，运行时 provider 注册使用本次实际地址，面板显示回退结果。国内模型仅使用国内账号。 端口在预留与监听之间被别的进程抢走时，该网关本次启动失败：它的模型组会被摘掉，连接检查报出失败原因，面板提示重启宿主。重启后 host 重新读注册表，请求才会落到新地址上。 ## 数据与出网 只读三家 App 的本机登录文件，不写回登录状态。provider 通过运行时注册接入，不改写宿主 provider 配置；插件设置仍由宿主持久化至 profile。令牌仅在插件进程中使用，并发往对应厂商接口。网关仅监听 `127.0.0.1`；面板资源与 RPC 只接受实际回环对端，不信任代理转发头，因此远程浏览器不能直接使用面板。插件不直接管理或删除宿主会话记录。插件自管数据目录 `~/.dsh/dsh-wtq-pool/`（设了 `DSH_HOME` 则用它）里另有两个文件：`checkin-slots.json` 记录已领取的签到时段，先写临时文件再改名，只保留三天；`doctor.txt` 是最近一次连接检查的报告。 同一台机器上的其他进程可以调用这些回环端点，从而消耗已登录账号的额度。重启后回复缺失时应同时检查插件日志与宿主持久化日志。 令牌只会发往以下主机： - WorkBuddy：`copilot.tencent.com`、`www.codebuddy.cn`、`www.codebuddy.ai`、`www.workbuddy.ai`、`www.workbuddy.cn` - Trae：`api.trae.cn`、`solo.trae.cn`、`trae-api-cn.mchost.guru`、`coresg-normal.trae.ai`、`growsg-normal.trae.ai` - Qoder：`gateway.qoder.com.cn`、`openapi.qoder.com.cn`、`api3.qoder.sh`、`openapi.qoder.sh` 插件不发送遥测。面板外链仅在用户点击时打开。 ## 开发 ```sh pnpm install pnpm run build # 产出 lib/（宿主半为 ESM，客户端半为 CJS） pnpm run typecheck # 宿主半 pnpm run typecheck:client pnpm test # Node 自带测试，离线回归 ``` `src/host.ts` 是引擎（账号发现、池、网关、面板通道），`src/index.ts` 是 Cordis 入口（设置 schema、provider 注册、面板路由），`src/pi-compat.ts` 把宿主能力适配成引擎已在用的那套调用。`renderer/` 是面板本体：`index.html`、`panel.js`、`panel.css`，原生 JS，无构建步骤，由 `src/web-panel.ts` 挂在宿主 web 服务上，以同源 iframe 提供给插件页卡片；`src/client/` 是 React 半，只有嵌这个 iframe 的插件页卡片（`index.tsx`）和输入框工具栏读数（`composer.tsx`）。`lib/` 由 `tsdown` 产出，`package.json` 的 `files` 与版本库都带着它，修改 `src/` 后须重建并提交。 与宿主无关的核心模块： | 模块 | 职责 | | --- | --- | | `loopback.ts` | 回环端点的安全模型、响应写入、中继泵送（pumpToResponse / relayStreamOf）与报错脱敏 | | `accounts.ts` | WorkBuddy 登录文件解析、令牌加解密、账号池与冷却 | | `upstream.ts` | WorkBuddy 上游客户端、错误分类、限流重置解析 | | `catalog.ts` | 模型目录与静态兜底列表 | | `shim.ts` | WorkBuddy 网关的 OpenAI 兼容端点 | | `at-rest.ts` | 5.6+ 密封登录字

plugins.description: DeepSeek Harness plugin that blocks agent edits that weaken tests, such as .skip, deleted or watered-down assertions.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-protect-tests

English | [中文](README_zh.md)

Tell an agent "make the tests pass" and sometimes it does exactly that, just not the way you meant. A failing test gets `.skip`. An assertion gets commented out. `expect(total).toBe(42)` turns into `expect(total).toBeDefined()`. The run goes green and the bug is still there.

This [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) plugin looks at every edit to a test file before it's applied, comparing the old text with the new. If the change makes the tests check less, the edit is refused and the model is told what it did:
(haha claude is so useful i mean like idk)
```
dsh-protect-tests blocked this change to src/sum.test.ts because it makes the tests check less:
- replaces specific assertions with existence/truthiness checks (0 → 1): `expect(sum(1, 2)).toBeDefined()`
Tests should keep failing until the code is fixed. Fix the implementation instead, or make
the test more accurate without weakening it. If the test itself is wrong (the requirement
changed, or it tested a bug), tell the user which test you are changing and why, then
repeat the identical call once to confirm.
```

## Install

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-protect-tests
```

That's the `web` profile, the browser UI you start with `dsh web`. If you run DSH another way, use `headless` (scripts and CI) or `acp` (editor integrations) instead. Each profile keeps its own plugin list, so add it to every profile you use. It's on as soon as it's installed. Remove it with `dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-protect-tests`.

### From a clone

To try local changes, build a tarball and install that:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/acus9345/dsh-protect-tests
cd dsh-protect-tests
npm install
npm pack
dsh plugin --profile web add ./dsh-protect-tests-0.2.0.tgz
```

## What it notices

- **New skips.** `it.skip`, `test.only`, `xit`, `xdescribe`, `@pytest.mark.skip` / `xfail`, `@unittest.skip`, `t.Skip()`, `@Disabled`, `#[ignore]`, and the equivalents in xUnit, RSpec, PHPUnit and XCTest.
- **Fewer tests or assertions.** Removing a test case, or removing two or more assertions in one edit. Both thresholds are configurable.
- **Assertions that can't fail.** `expect(true).toBe(true)`, `assert True`, `assertEquals(x, x)`, `assert!(true)`.
- **Commented-out assertions.**
- **Swallowed failures.** Wrapping assertions in an empty `catch {}` or `except AssertionError: pass`.
- **Weaker assertions.** Swapping a specific check for `toBeDefined()`, `toBeTruthy()`, `assert.ok(x)`, `is not None` and the like.
- **Deleted test files.** `rm`, `git rm` or `unlink` on a test file or test folder from the shell.
- **A test script that can't fail.** Changing `"test"` in `package.json` to `echo`, `exit 0`, `... || true`, or adding `--passWithNoTests`.

On Windows, PowerShell deletes (`Remove-Item`, `del`, `rd`) count too.

Test files are found by name: `*.test.*`, `*.spec.*`, `*_test.*`, `test_*.py`, `*Test.java`, `conftest.py`, anything under `tests/`, `__tests__/`, `spec/` or `e2e/`, and so on. You can change the list.

Normal test work isn't affected. Adding tests, adding assertions, renaming, refactoring setup code and fixing a typo in a test name all go through without a word. Refactors that look like losses on paper also go through, for example folding five near-identical tests into one `test.each` / `@pytest.mark.parametrize` / `t.Run` table, or merging three `toBe` checks into one `toEqual({...})` or a helper like `expectUser(...)`.

## When the test really is wrong

Sometimes it is. The requirement changed, or the test was asserting the bug. In that case the model is asked to tell you which test it's changing and why, then repeat the same call once to confirm. The repeat goes through. So the guard never fully blocks legitimate work. It just won't let a weakened test slip past without being mentioned in the conversation. If you'd rather approve these yourself, use `mode: ask`.

## What it won't catch

It works on patterns, not on meaning. If the model changes `toBe(4)` to `toBe(5)` to match a wrong result, that looks like an ordinary edit and gets through. Rewriting the logic of a test so it no longer exercises the bug also gets through. It covers the lazy shortcuts, which turn out to be most of them, but it's no substitute for reading the diff.

## Settings

The easy way: open **Plugins** in DSH's sidebar, click **dsh-protect-tests**, change what you want and press **Save**. It applies to the next tool call, no restart needed.

Or add a row like this to `~/.dsh/profiles/<profile>/cordis.patch.yml`, or to `~/.dsh/cordis.patch.yml` for every profile. Keys you leave out keep their defaults.

```yaml
- id: protect-tests
  config:
    mode: deny                  # or `ask` for an approval prompt
    testFiles: ['*.test.*', '**/tests/**', '!tests/fixtures/**']   # replaces the default list
    minAssertionsRemoved: 2
    minTestsRemoved: 1
    disabledSignals: []         # skip, fewer-assertions, fewer-tests, trivial-assert,
                                # commented-assert, swallowed-failure, weaker-assert
    guardDeletes: true          # watch rm / git rm of test files
    guardTestScript: true       # watch package.json "test"
    allowIdenticalRetry: true   # false: a refusal is final
    shellTools: [bash, pwsh]   # pwsh is the shell DSH uses on Windows
```

## Development

```sh
npm install
npm test           # detector unit tests
npm run test:e2e   # real dsh runs against a scripted local model, no API key needed
```

The install test runs `dsh plugin add`, which needs `pnpm` on your PATH.

MIT licensed. Written by [acus9345](https://github.com/acus9345). Bug reports and ideas are welcome in the issues.

plugins.description: OpenAI-compatible image generation for DeepSeek Harness — text-to-image, image editing and batch generation, rendered straight in the conversation.
plugins.readme_text:
# Cture Image **Image generation for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai), without leaving the conversation.** Text-to-image · image editing · batch generation — through any OpenAI-compatible images API, rendered straight into the chat and saved to your workspace. [![CI](https://github.com/Cikian/dsh-cture-image/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/Cikian/dsh-cture-image/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/Cikian/dsh-cture-image?sort=semver)](https://github.com/Cikian/dsh-cture-image/releases) [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE) [![Node](https://img.shields.io/badge/node-%3E%3D20-3c873a.svg)](package.json) [中文文档](README.zh.md) · [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md) · [Releases](https://github.com/Cikian/dsh-cture-image/releases) *Prompt: “一只戴圆框眼镜的橘猫坐在书桌前敲代码…扁平化矢量插画风格” — generated by this plugin (`gpt-image-2.5-sunburst`, 2K, 16:9, high quality). It reported the real pixel size: 1672×941.*
--- ## Features - **Three tasks, one tool** — `generate` (text-to-image), `edit` (image-to-image and inpainting, with an optional mask) and `batch` (many prompts in one call, bounded concurrency). - **Pictures in the conversation** — every result comes back as a real image content block backed by a durable attachment, so it displays inline and can be downloaded. The untouched original bytes are written to your workspace as well. - **Full parameter control** — model, quality, resolution tier, aspect ratio, count, save directory and whether to append rendering guidance. - **Configured in the Plugins page** — the bundle ships a settings form with a connectivity test that reports each step (`✓` / `✕`) before you save. The API key is stored on the host and never sent back to the browser. - **Agent-drivable** — an `imagegen_config` tool lets the model inspect and change the same configuration from the conversation. - **A proper DSH bundle** — appears under **Installed** in the Plugins page, can be toggled like any other bundle, and applies to every preset and session. ## Requirements | | | |---|---| | DeepSeek Harness | **0.2.x** (desktop app or `dsh web`); built against the 0.2 bundle + client-module API | | Node.js | **≥ 20** (only for the development scripts — the plugin itself runs inside DSH) | | An image endpoint | Any **OpenAI-compatible** images API (`POST /images/generations`, `POST /images/edits`) and a key for it | ## Install ### From npm ```powershell # Desktop app (profile: desktop) dsh plugin --profile desktop add @cikian/dsh-cture-image # CLI web app (profile: web) dsh plugin --profile web add @cikian/dsh-cture-image ``` ### From a release artifact (offline) Download `cikian-dsh-cture-image-1.0.0.tgz` from the [Releases](https://github.com/Cikian/dsh-cture-image/releases) page, then point the plugin manager at the file: ```powershell dsh plugin --profile desktop add .\cikian-dsh-cture-image-1.0.0.tgz ``` Both routes install the same package. The tarball carries the runtime files only — no API key, and nothing to configure before it runs. > **Restart DSH after installing or moving the plugin.** The host half mounts > immediately, but a bundle's client half (the settings form, the image view) is > composed into the page at boot. Installing into a page that is already open is > the one situation where the plugin reports *running* while its UI is missing. > See [Troubleshooting](#troubleshooting). Verify the install: open **Plugins → Installed** — *Cture Image* should be listed and switched on. Its detail page then shows the configuration form. ## Configure Open **Plugins → Installed → Cture Image**. The form is rendered between the description and the plugin's rows. | Field | Meaning | |---|---| | **Base URL** | Root of the OpenAI-compatible images API. Ships pointing at `https://api.cikhub.com/v1`; any compatible endpoint works | | **API key** | Your key. Stored on the host, shown back only as `***set***` | | **Model** | Default model; the dropdown is filled from `GET /models`, and free text is accepted | | **Quality** | `low` · `medium` · `high` · `xhigh` · `max` | | **Resolution** | `1K` · `2K` · `4K` (expressed as pixel sizes, see [compatibility](#endpoint-compatibility)) | | **Aspect ratio** | `1:1` · `2:3` · `4:3` · `3:4` · `16:9` · `9:16` · `21:9` · `9:21` | | **Count** | Images per prompt, 1–8 | | **Save directory** | Workspace-relative directory for the originals (default `saved-images`) | | **Test connectivity** | Probes the endpoint with the *draft* values and reports each step without saving | | **Test with one image** | Renders one cheap 1024×1024 image to prove the model and quota work | **Where the configuration lives.** In `config.json` beside the installed package, written atomically. Precedence is `config.json` → the bundle patch row's `config` → the built-in defaults in `lib/host.js`. It is deliberately **not** part of the published package, so shipping the plugin never ships a key: ``` /node_modules/@cikian/dsh-cture-image/config.json ``` Three ways to change it: the settings form, the agent (`imagegen_config action:"set" fields:{…}`), or editing that file directly. The API key is never returned to the browser — the form only learns that one is set. ## Usage Talk to the agent; no commands to remember. ``` 画一只戴眼镜的猫，插画风格 把 saved-images/20261014-085102-readme-1.png 的背景换成夜晚 批量出 3 个封面候选 ``` ### `generate_image` | `action` | What it does | |---|---| | `generate` *(default)* | Text-to-image: `POST /images/generations` | | `edit` | Image-to-image / inpainting from local files (`image_paths`, optional `mask_path`): `POST /images/edits` as multipart | | `batch` | One call, many prompts (`prompts`), concurrency from the `concurrency` setting | | Parameter | Default | Notes | |---|---|---| | `prompt` | — | Any language; rendering guidance (ratio, pixels, quality, model strengths) is appended unless `optimize_prompt` is off | | `model` | `gpt-image-2.5-sunburst` | `gpt-image-2.5-flare` suits batch sketches and cover candidates; `gpt-image-2.5` is general purpose | | `quality` | `high` | `low` · `medium` · `high` · `xhigh` · `max` | | `resolution` | `1K` | `1K` · `2K` · `4K`, mapped to pixel sizes that are multiples of 16 | | `aspect_ratio` | `16:9` | 8 supported ratios | | `count` | `1` | 1–8 per prompt | | `save_dir` | `saved-images` | Workspace-relative | | `optimize_prompt` | `true` | Append the rendering guidance to your prompt | Every generated image is (1) written to `/saved-images/--.png` as the exact bytes the endpoint returned, (2) attached as a durable attachment and returned as an image content block, and (3) reported in the result with its real pixel size, byte size, attachment id and workspace path. ### `imagegen_config` | `action` | What it does | |---|---| | `get` | Show the effective configuration | | `set` | Validate, persist and apply new values (`fields: { … }`) | | `models` | List the image models the endpoint advertises | ## Endpoint compatibility The plugin targets the OpenAI images API, but the details vary between providers and relays. What has been observed in practice, and how the plugin reacts: - **Pixel sizes, not tier names.** Some endpoints ignore `size: "1K"` and `aspect_ratio` entirely, so the plugin always sends concrete pixel dimensions (`1024x1024`, `1536x1024`, `1024x1536`, …) and expresses the ratio that way. - **Some providers cap resolution around 1.6 MP** and silently scale a large request down (`2560×1440` → `1672×941`). The tool reports the **actual** size it received, so a capped result is visible instead of implied. - **Extreme ratios may be clamped** server-side; `21:9` can come back close to 2:1. - **`edit` needs an endpoint that accepts multipart uploads** at `/images/edits`. If yours does not, `generate` still works. - **Models are whatever your endpoint exposes.** The built-in list is a hint, not a constraint — use `i

plugins.description: Reverse engineer anything with agents, from app behavior down to native binaries.
plugins.readme_text:
**English** · [简体中文](docs/readme/README_zh.md) · [繁體中文](docs/readme/README_zh-TW.md) · [日本語](docs/readme/README_ja.md) · [한국어](docs/readme/README_ko.md) · [Türkçe](docs/readme/README_tr.md) · [Русский](docs/readme/README_ru.md) · [Tiếng Việt](docs/readme/README_vi.md) · [ไทย](docs/readme/README_th.md) · [Deutsch](docs/readme/README_de.md) · [Español](docs/readme/README_es.md) · [Français](docs/readme/README_fr.md) · [Українська](docs/readme/README_uk.md) · [Polski](docs/readme/README_pl.md) · [Português (Brasil)](docs/readme/README_pt-BR.md) · [العربية](docs/readme/README_ar.md) · [فارسی](docs/readme/README_fa.md) · [Bahasa Indonesia](docs/readme/README_id.md) · [Italiano](docs/readme/README_it.md) · [Ελληνικά](docs/readme/README_el.md) # REA: Reverse Engineer Anything ### One MCP for reverse engineering across binaries, applications, and runtime behavior. **See a feature you like. Understand how it works, down to the binary level.** [![npm version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/rea-agents?style=flat-square&color=cb3837)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/rea-agents) [![MCP tool catalog](https://img.shields.io/badge/MCP-tool_catalog-5c4ee5?style=flat-square)](docs/mcp-contracts.md#generated-catalog) [![Node.js requirements](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-requirements-339933?style=flat-square&logo=nodedotjs&logoColor=white)](#what-you-can-analyze) [![skills.sh](https://skills.sh/b/morluto/rea?style=flat-square)](https://skills.sh/morluto/rea/reverse-engineer-anything) [![MIT license](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-f4c430?style=flat-square)](LICENSE) [![Discord](https://img.shields.io/discord/1556595354999332884?logo=discord&logoColor=white&label=Discord&color=5865F2)](https://discord.gg/GkcryMnJDM) **[Website](https://reareverse.com/) · [Guides](https://reareverse.com/guides/) · [Showcases](https://reareverse.com/showcase/)** [Quick start](#quick-start) · [How REA works](#how-rea-works) · [What you can analyze](#what-you-can-analyze) · [Showcases](#showcases) · [FAQ](#faq) · [Documentation](#documentation) npx rea-agents setup
> [!IMPORTANT] > Get REA from [morluto/rea](https://github.com/morluto/rea), > [reareverse.com](https://reareverse.com/), or the [rea-agents npm package](https://www.npmjs.com/package/rea-agents). > Follow the installation and release links from these official sources. A similar > repository name or copied README does not establish that a download is official.




Join the Reverse Engineering Community
Discord · Q&A · Show and Tell

--- See a feature in an app that you want in your own product? Ask your agent to investigate it with REA. It can inspect the app without its source code, explain how the feature works, show the evidence, and build a version for your project. REA connects your agent to tools for inspecting native binaries, JavaScript and Electron apps, .NET assemblies, and websites. You can also use the same tools from your terminal. Analysis runs locally, and results include the evidence and limitations behind each conclusion. Setup registers REA with your agent and installs matching workflow instructions. Native analysis can use an existing Hopper, Ghidra, or IDA installation; setup can optionally install Hopper with approval. Static JavaScript analysis needs no native analysis engine. > **[Visit the REA website](https://reareverse.com/)** for setup instructions, illustrated guides, and real case studies. ## Quick start On Linux, Ghidra, JADX, firmware tool launches and static JavaScript/Electron analysis require a procps-compatible `ps` on REA's `PATH` for process ownership checks. Recovery steps are in `docs/installation.md` under "Linux owned-process prerequisite". ### Set up your agent With Node.js and npm installed, run: ```bash npx rea-agents setup ``` Choose your agents, review the proposed changes, and approve them. Setup adds REA's MCP server and matching workflow instructions, with backups of existing configuration. Restart your agent afterward. Setup supports Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, Grok Build and [other agents](docs/installation.md#supported-agents). See [installation and setup](docs/installation.md) for provider configuration and manual MCP registration. ### Ask your agent ```text Understand how search works in the Notes app, show me the evidence, and build a similar feature for my project. ``` Replace Notes with your target app and the feature you want to understand. ### Use the terminal Inspect an extracted JavaScript/Electron app directory or ASAR: ```bash npx -y rea-agents@latest analyze-javascript-application /absolute/path/to/app --json ``` The result includes modules, imports, Electron boundaries and their evidence. Replace the path with your target, such as `"D:/apps/example"` on Windows. To install the `rea` command for regular use: ```bash npm install --global rea-agents rea --help ``` For native analysis, configure a provider first. See the [CLI and Evidence guide](docs/cli.md) for native commands, provider selection, snapshots and scripting. ### Update REA REA changes quickly, and new releases include frequent bug fixes. Keep your installation up to date. For a CLI installed with `npm install --global` or `bun add --global`: ```bash rea update ``` Bun global updates require Bun 1.2.17 or later. With an older Bun release, upgrade Bun manually before running `rea update`. To refresh your agent registrations and skill, run the setup command printed by the update. If you use `npx`, update your agent setup with: ```bash npx rea-agents@latest setup ``` Review the setup changes and restart your agent. For one-off CLI commands, use `npx rea-agents@latest` followed by the command. With Bun, use `bunx rea-agents@latest` in place of `npx rea-agents@latest`. ## How REA works Your agent calls REA through MCP to inspect the target and trace relevant code. REA returns findings with their evidence. The agent uses them to ask follow-up questions, explain the behavior, or write and test an implementation. CLI commands use the same workflows. ![REA investigation flow: your agent asks about a local target, REA inspects and traces it using analysis tools, and the agent uses the returned code, references and unknowns to explain, implement and test.](website/public/assets/figures/rea-investigation-flow.svg) [Open the full-size figure](website/public/assets/figures/rea-investigation-flow.svg). ## What you can analyze REA requires Node.js 22.x (>=22.19), 24.x (>=24.11), or 26+, plus npm. Additional tools and host support depend on the target: | Target | What REA returns | Requirements and guide | | ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | Native binaries | Pseudocode, assembly, strings, symbols, calls and references | Hopper, Ghidra or IDA; [native analysis](docs/native-investigation.md) | | Offline ELF layout

plugins.description: DSH 1.5 上下文治理：折叠工具结果、保持提示词缓存命中、接管宿主可写请求（不再需要 dsh-llm 文件补丁）。仅支持 DSH 1.5，后续会跟进更新。 / Context governance for DSH 1.5: folds tool results, keeps the prompt cache warm, takes over the writable-request path. DSH 1.5 only; newer releases will follow.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-context-reclaim **Tool results are reclaimed before they enter history, so the prompt cache never goes cold.** > ⚠️ **DSH 1.5 only** (`>=0.1.5-rc.2 <0.2.0`). Newer DSH releases will be supported in follow-up updates. > 🟢 **Collision risk: very low.** It occupies **5 server-side seams and 0 client slots** — measured alongside the **19 same-track plugins** among the 44 installed here, with no conflict, and it takes **no `chain` slot** (the only kind that makes plugins displace each other). See [Compatibility](#compatibility). [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE) [![DSH](https://img.shields.io/badge/DSH-1.5-8a2be2.svg)](#compatibility) [![Platform](https://img.shields.io/badge/platform-desktop%20%7C%20web-lightgrey.svg)](#compatibility) **English** · [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md)
--- ## What this is A DSH session's context is not blown up by the conversation; it is blown up by **tool results**: a single `read` of several hundred lines, a single `pwsh` dumping a wall of logs, a system prompt repeated verbatim every turn. Once this content has entered the history, the only thing left is for the compactor to operate on it after the fact — and compaction has to rewrite already-committed history, which knocks out the whole server-side prefix cache and makes every compaction more expensive than the last. `dsh-context-reclaim` moves to a different position: it handles them **before the tool result is appended to history**, and it never rewrites content that has already been committed. So the prefix cache is never invalidated because of this plugin. It hooks into 5 seams: | Seam | What it does | Default | |---|---|---| | `tools/post-execute` | Purify a tool result the moment it is produced + bound it by content type, inserting a retrieval pointer at the truncation point | on | | `system-prompt/assemble` | Fold the tool definition surface, stabilize the order of prefix sections, truncate over-long description lines | on | | `tools/pre-execute` | Duplicate-edit interception (a second identical edit to the same content of the same file is rejected outright) | on | | `session/event` | Compaction-summary integrity audit (warns when a compaction summary is missing sections) | on | | `llm/stream` | One cost-attribution line per request, printing route / prompt / cache hit / output | on | --- ## 1. Tool-result purification and bounding This is the core. Every time a tool call returns, the plugin first performs **lossless purification**, then **bounding**. ### Lossless purification Collapses ANSI escape sequences, strips trailing whitespace, normalizes CR. This step is pure purification and loses no information. It only acts when the content meets **both** thresholds: length ≥ 32 characters, and a reduction ratio after purification ≥ 0.2%. Small results are not touched at all. Turn it off: `config.noise = false`, or the environment variable `DSH_RECLAIM_NOISE=0`. ### Bounding by content type Different types of tool results have completely different tolerances. The plugin sorts tools into three classes: | Class | Tools covered | Head / tail kept | Per-line cap | Total character cap | |---|---|---|---|---| | **Read-only** | `read` `grep` `glob` `codegraph_*` `lsp_*` | 80 lines / 12 lines | 512 | 160 | | **Side-effecting** | `pwsh` `bash` `docker_*` `job_output` | 40 lines / 40 lines | 1024 | 256 | | **Faithful** | `web_fetch` `web_search` `knowledge_*` `read_image` `pilot_snapshot` | left exactly as-is | — | — | Tools it does not recognize are treated as **faithful** — better to save nothing than to cause unintended damage. Wherever content was truncated, a retrieval pointer is inserted telling you how much of the original is left and how it can be retrieved, rather than dropping it silently. The trigger threshold for bounding is "saves more than 5%"; if it does not save much, nothing is touched. Turn it off: `config.bounded = false`, or the environment variable `DSH_RECLAIM_BOUNDED=0`. > **About oversized results**: content above `config.maxInlineBytes` (default 50000) is handed to the spill mechanism to be written to disk. This requires the spill plugin to be installed in your profile — without it, this threshold has no effect and over-limit content passes through unchanged. ### The faithful allowlist The lists for all three tool classes can be replaced wholesale in the configuration: ```yaml - id: reclaim config: readOnlyTools: ['read', 'grep', 'glob'] # a full-table replacement, not an append sideEffectTools: ['pwsh', 'bash'] faithfulTools: ['web_fetch', 'web_search'] ``` Note that this is a **full-table replacement**, not a per-field merge — writing only `headLines` will lose the character caps. Either write the whole table or write none of it. --- ## 2. Tool definition surface folding At the start of every session, DSH stuffs the complete definitions (name, description, parameter schema) of every available tool into the system prompt. With dozens of plugins installed, this block can account for a large proportion of it, while most of those tools will not be used at all in the current turn. By default the plugin **folds** this part: it keeps the full definitions of the most frequently used tools and compresses the rest into a one-line list (name + one-line description, no parameter schema). **A folded tool is still callable.** The one-line list only removes the schema from the prompt — the tool itself stays registered with the host, so the model can still find it with `search_tools`, call it straight away with `invoke_tool`, or make it resident again with `load_plugin`. There is no `load_tools` tool; `search_tools` + `invoke_tool` is the pair. If you would rather keep every schema in the prompt, turn the folding off (next line). Turn it off: `config.foldTools = false`, or the environment variable `DSH_RECLAIM_TOOL_FOLD=0`. --- ## 3. Prefix stabilization A server-side prefix cache only hits when the **prefix is byte-for-byte unchanged**. Yet the system prompt inherently carries a pile of things that change every turn: token counts, timestamps, session sequence numbers. By default the plugin flattens these volatile numbers and reorders the sections so that stable sections come first and volatile ones last. Each reorder prints one `[reclaim/section-order]` line in the log, telling you which sections were moved. --- ## 4. Truncating over-long description lines The system prompt occasionally contains a single exceptionally long description line (long comments written by some plugins). Lines above the threshold (not exposed in `config`; the environment variable `DSH_RECLAIM_PROMPT_LINE_MAX`, default 120 characters) are truncated, and the line numbers that were truncated are printed to the log. --- ## 5. Duplicate-edit interception If the model issues exactly the same modification to the same content of the same file twice in a row, the second one is intercepted and an explanation is returned — such a call is almost certainly a meaningless duplicate that burns a whole round trip for nothing. Log line: `[reclaim/dedup-deny]`. Turn it off: the environment variable `DSH_RECLAIM_DEDUP_DENY=0`. --- ## 6. Compaction-summary integrity audit If the summary produced by the compactor is truncated by the output budget, it **silently** becomes shorter — you receive no notice at all, the next turn simply starts with a piece of the context missing. After every compaction the plugin audits whether the summary contains the structural sections it should have, and warns when any are missing: ``` [reclaim/summary-audit] ⚠️ 摘要缺 3/8 段 ``` It **only warns, it does not modify the summary**. What actually prevents summaries from being truncated is [`dsh-aux-degrade`](#-with-dsh-aux-degrade-the-context-governance-pair--install-both-together); see the interaction section below. --- ## 7. Cost attribution One line is printed at the end of every request: ``` [reclaim/usage] route=aux prompt=12043 hit=11890 miss=153 out=204 purpose=compaction ``` `hit` / `miss` are the prefix-cache hit and miss character counts, and `purpose` is the purpose

plugins.description: DeepSeek Harness plugin that stops agents from running shell commands that wait for input or never exit.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-block-hanging-commands

English | [中文](README_zh.md)

If you've used an agent for a while you've probably seen this. It runs `git commit` without `-m`, or `npm run dev`, or `python3` with nothing after it, and the turn just sits there. The command is waiting for a keyboard nobody is typing on. Usually the tool times out, the model learns nothing, and then it tries something just as bad.

This plugin for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) reads each shell command before it runs. If the command would wait for input or never exit, it doesn't run it. The model gets told why and what to run instead, so it can fix the call in the same step.

```
dsh-block-hanging-commands stopped `git commit` before it ran, because `git commit`
without a message opens an editor, so the tool call would just sit there until it timed out.
Instead: pass the message: `git commit -m "<message>"` (or `--no-edit` when amending).
(rule: git-editor)
```

## Install

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-block-hanging-commands
```

That's the `web` profile, the browser UI you start with `dsh web`. If you run DSH another way, use `headless` (scripts and CI) or `acp` (editor integrations) instead. Each profile keeps its own plugin list, so add it to every profile you use. That's all the setup there is. The plugin ships its own patch layer, so it's on as soon as it's installed.

To remove it: `dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-block-hanging-commands`.

### From a clone

To try local changes, build a tarball and install that:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/acus9345/dsh-block-hanging-commands
cd dsh-block-hanging-commands
npm install
npm pack
dsh plugin --profile web add ./dsh-block-hanging-commands-0.2.0.tgz
```

## What it catches

| Rule | Examples | What the model is told to do instead |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `editor` | `vim`, `nano`, `emacs`, `code --wait`, `subl -w` | use the edit tools or `sed -i` |
| `git-editor` | `git commit` or `git tag -a` without `-m` | pass `-m` / `--no-edit` |
| `git-interactive` | `git rebase -i`, `git add -p` | a plain rebase or `--autosquash` with `GIT_SEQUENCE_EDITOR=:`; `git add <path>` |
| `repl` | `python`, `node`, `psql mydb`, `redis-cli`, `sqlite3 db` | `-c "..."`, a script file, or a heredoc |
| `server` | `npm run dev`, `vite`, `next dev`, `flask run`, `rails s` | `run_in_background: true`, or `timeout` |
| `watch` | `jest --watch`, `tsc -w`, `cargo watch`, `nodemon` | run once without the watch flag |
| `follow` | `tail -f`, `journalctl -f`, `kubectl logs -f`, `docker logs -f` | `tail -n 200`, `--since` |
| `remote-shell` | `ssh host` with no command | pass the command; `-o BatchMode=yes` |
| `container-tty` | `docker run -it`, `docker exec -it`, `kubectl exec -it` | drop `-it` |
| `tui` | `htop`, `top`, `lazygit`, `tig`, `ncdu` | the batch version (`top -bn1`, `git log`) |
| `prompt` / `login` | `npm init` without `-y`, `crontab -e`, `gh auth login`, `aws configure` | the non-interactive flags, or ask the user |
| `pager`, `tty-prompt` | `less file`, `sudo` asking for a password | only on a PTY shell, see below |

It looks through the usual wrappers (`sudo`, `env`, `nohup`, `npx`, `pnpm exec`, `uv run`, `bash -c '...'`) and handles pipes, `&&` chains, heredocs and redirects. So `cd app && npm run dev` is caught, but `echo q | python3` and `python3 < script.py` are not, because their input is already there. `timeout 30 npm run dev` gets through, and so does any call made with `run_in_background: true`. In both cases the command is going to end or detach anyway. A dev server, watcher or `tail -f` called with the shell tool's own `timeoutMs` also gets through, since that bounds it the same way. An editor or prompt still doesn't, because a timeout just leaves it waiting in the background.

It works on Windows too, where DSH runs commands through PowerShell (`pwsh`) instead of bash. There it also knows `npm.cmd`, full paths like `C:\Python312\python.exe`, the `&` call operator and `Get-Content -Wait`.

I tried hard to keep false positives down. `psql -c "select 1"`, `node script.js`, `vim -es`, `git commit -F msg.txt`, `top -bn1`, `ssh host uptime` and `--help` / `--version` on anything all pass.

## Settings

The easy way: open **Plugins** in DSH's sidebar, click **dsh-block-hanging-commands**, change what you want and press **Save**. It applies to the next tool call, no restart needed.

Or put a row like this in `~/.dsh/profiles/<profile>/cordis.patch.yml`, or in `~/.dsh/cordis.patch.yml` to cover every profile. Keys you leave out keep their defaults.

```yaml
- id: block-hanging-commands
  config:
    mode: deny             # or `ask` to get an approval prompt instead of a refusal
    tools: [bash, pwsh]    # shell tool names to inspect (pwsh is the Windows shell)
    pty: false             # set true if your shell tool runs on a PTY (dsh-tool-bash-persistent)
    disabledRules: []      # e.g. [server] if you really want the model starting dev servers
    allowPatterns: []      # regexes, e.g. ['^make serve$']
```

`pty` matters because without a terminal, `less` and `git log` don't page, and `sudo` fails instead of prompting. So those rules only switch on when the shell really is a PTY.

## How it works

The plugin hooks `tools/pre-execute`. It tokenises the command itself (no shell is spawned), checks each simple command against the rules, and returns `deny` with the reason text if one matches. Nothing runs and nothing is rewritten. The model still decides what to do next. It's just deciding with better information.

## Development

```sh
npm install
npm test           # unit tests for the command parser and rules
npm run test:e2e   # boots real dsh against a scripted local model, no API key needed
```

The install test runs `dsh plugin add`, which needs `pnpm` on your PATH.

The e2e suite also packs the plugin and installs it with `dsh plugin add`, the same way a user would, to make sure the published package actually loads.

MIT licensed. Written by [acus9345](https://github.com/acus9345). Bug reports and ideas are welcome in the issues.

plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-sciwork · DSH 科研模式

> 给 [DSH](https://github.com/deepseek-ai)（DeepSeek Harness）装上一整套「做科研」的工作台：一个叫**科研模式**的 agent 预设，加上一个本机的实体科研库。

[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-yellow.svg)](https://opensource.org/licenses/MIT)
[![DSH plugin](https://img.shields.io/badge/DSH-plugin-4B6BFB.svg)](https://github.com/58catmiao/dsh-sciwork)
[![zero dependency](https://img.shields.io/badge/dependencies-0-brightgreen.svg)](https://github.com/58catmiao/dsh-sciwork)

版本 0.1.0 · MIT · 作者 [58catmiao](https://github.com/58catmiao) · 仓库 <https://github.com/58catmiao/dsh-sciwork>

**English:** [README.en.md](README.en.md)

---

## 这是什么

`dsh-sciwork` 不是一个"帮你查文献"的对话框，而是一套**落在你硬盘上、可被别的工具打开**的科研工作台。装上它，你会同时得到四样东西：

1. **一个 agent 预设「科研模式」**——它把绘图、写作、文献、期刊规范四条线收进同一个工作流：先找证据，再动手；出图走 Origin 真机，稿子里引用的每一条文献都必须带 DOI 或 URL。
2. **一个本机实体科研库**——一棵普通目录（课题 / 图表 / 数据 / 草稿 / 文献 / 期刊档案 / 投稿），配套一个 Python 引擎 `research.py` 和一个登记索引。
3. **12 份期刊投稿档案**——Nature、Science、Cell、IEEE Trans、ACS、Elsevier 通用、MDPI、PLOS ONE、中文核心、CNKI 学位论文、GB/T 7714、通用学位论文，各自的数值要求、条款与出处摘要。
4. **一个「科研库」可视面板 + 一组技能**——面板七个页签，只读为主、能筛能导入能归档；技能负责把"该怎么画、该怎么写、该怎么引"固化成纪律。

**权威来源永远是文件系统。** 索引只是缓存，面板的写入永远走库脚本，不直接改索引。所以科研库随时可以整目录打包带迁移，也可以直接用资源管理器、Git、别的编辑器去碰。

- 宿主半边是纯 Node ESM，**零 npm 依赖**。
- 客户端是手写的单文件 Web 客户端，**没有构建步骤**。
- 出图能力依赖上游开源插件 [dsh-origin-plugin](https://github.com/Fantasality/dsh-origin-plugin)（MIT，作者 Fantasality）。**本仓库不包含它**，只带适配技能。详见〈与 dsh-origin-plugin 的关系〉。

## 安装

```bash
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add dsh-sciwork
```

插件市场里点安装，走的也是同一条路径。装完**重启 Harness**。

装完后你会多出：

- 一个 ID 为 `research` 的 agent 预设「科研模式」（可直接在会话里选）；
- 侧栏多一个面板入口「科研库」；
- 一条精确注册的只读路由 `/api/research/call`（面板靠它取快照与执行动作）；
- 五个技能进入技能目录。

> 前置：本机有 Node（宿主半边与自检脚本用它）与一个可用的 Python 3 解释器（科研库引擎 `research.py` 用它）。**不要求 `python` 出现在 PATH 上**——启动器会按「显式配置 → `SCIWORK_PYTHON` → 库自己的 venv → Origin 插件目录的 venv → PATH」逐个探测。出图另需 Origin，见下文。

## 快速开始

### 1. 建库

```bash
# 先预检：不写任何文件，只报告缺什么
node scripts/install.mjs --verify-only

# 预检通过后建库
node scripts/install.mjs
```

安装脚本会建出库根目录、`.research/` 引擎与索引、`journals/` 期刊档案、`refs/` 文献库。库根默认是 `<用户目录>/Research`（Windows 即 `%USERPROFILE%\Research`），可用环境变量 `SCIWORK_LIBRARY` 改。

安装脚本的可用开关：

| 开关 | 说明 |
| --- | --- |
| `--verify-only` | 只检查，不写任何文件。 |
| `--library-root <dir>` | 指定库根，覆盖配置里的 `libraryRoot`。 |
| `--skip-library` | 不铺科研库骨架（只装插件半边）。 |
| `--force-skills` | 目标已存在且没有 `SKILL.md` 时也覆盖安装技能目录。 |

> 库根解析顺序：`--library-root` / 环境变量 `SCIWORK_LIBRARY`（旧名 `RESEARCH_LIBRARY` 兼容）→ 内核 `library/config.json` 的 `libraryRoot` → `<用户目录>/Research`。注意库内已有的 `.research/config.json` 里的 `libraryRoot` 也会覆盖环境变量——面板与引擎优先听库自己的配置。

### 2. 打开面板

在 DSH 侧栏点「科研库」。面板顶部一行写着当前库根路径与实时计数（课题 / 图 / 草稿 / 数据 / 文献 / 期刊档案 / 投稿 / 索引时间），下面是七个页签。

### 3. 让 agent 建课题

在会话里选「科研模式」预设，然后直接说：

> 建一个课题，叫 `zt-ceremic`，研究 ZrB₂-SiC 陶瓷的氧化行为。

agent 会走 `research.py new-project` 落目录，之后它画的每一张图、写的每一段结果，都会各自归位到该课题的 `figures/`、`origin/`、`data/`、`drafts/` 下。你也可以在面板里点「新建课题」自己建。

### 4. 出图

**面板自己不出图**（2026-10-13 起移除）。要出图，直接跟 agent 说：

> 把 `projects/zt-ceremic/data/` 里那组 XRD 数据画成对比图，按 MDPI 的排版要求。

agent 会走 Origin 真机绘图、核验、导出，并把图的溯源信息登记回库。

## 面板：七个页签各能做什么

侧栏「科研库」。页签七个（图表 / 草稿 / 文献 / 数据 / 期刊档案 / 投稿 / 归档），另有顶部的**计数行**与「命令台」弹层（两者都不是页签）：

| 页签 | 看什么 | 能做什么 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **计数行**（面板顶部，不是页签） | 库根路径、课题/图/草稿/数据/文献/期刊档案/投稿七项实时计数、索引时间、采集警告 | 点「刷新」重取快照；点「引导」走一遍带高亮的界面导览 |
| **图表** | 已登记的图，含每条图的登记溯源（数据源、脚本、生成时间）；按课题分组 | 看图、看 PDF 附带件、复制路径、重画、归档、删除 |
| **草稿** | `drafts/` 下的 Markdown 手稿 | 就地读；新建草稿；编辑保存；归档；删除 |
| **文献** | `refs/refs.json` 里的条目与 `refs/pdf/` 下的本地 PDF 附件 | 导入（必须带 DOI 或 URL 才登记，PDF 可选）、看 PDF、归档、删除 |
| **数据** | `data/` 下的数据文件（`.txt/.csv/.dat` 等）与按课题分组的分组头 | 预览行列、**数据变换**（6 个算子）、归档、删除 |
| **期刊档案** | 12 份档案的 id、严格度（high / medium / low）与更新日期 | 读条款与数值要求；筛选；归档 |
| **投稿** | `submissions/` 下的投稿记录（目标刊、状态、时间线） | 读记录；筛选；归档 |
| **归档** | `.research/archive/<时间戳>/` 里的批次清单 + 真删记录 | 整批 / 单文件「恢复」搬回原位；真删记录只留名字 |
| **命令台**（弹层，不是页签） | `research.py` 的子命令清单与参数表单 | 选命令 → 填参 → 执行 → 看 stdout / stderr / JSON 结果 |

**数据变换的 6 个算子**：`normalize`（归一化）、`baseline`（扣基线）、`smooth`（平滑）、`peaks`（找峰）、`integrate`（积分）、`linear`（线性变换）。每次变换都会在新表旁落一份溯源记录（`.research/transforms/<课题>/<表名>.json`），并把产物写进课题的 `tables/`。

**面板的边界，一句话说清**：能看、能筛、能导入、能归档、能删、能对表格做数据变换；**不出图**。所有写入都经库脚本落文件并登记，**面板自身不碰登记索引**。

## 配置

配置有两层，**库内 `<库根>/.research/config.json` 是权威**；环境变量用来告诉 DSH 去哪找库、用哪个 Python。

| 环境变量 | 默认值 | 说明 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `SCIWORK_LIBRARY` | `<用户目录>/Research` | 科研库根目录。改这里等于换库。 |
| `RESEARCH_LIBRARY` | 未设置 | 旧名，兼容保留；`SCIWORK_LIBRARY` 优先。 |
| `SCIWORK_PYTHON` | 依平台探测 | 跑 `research.py` 用的 Python 解释器。推荐显式指向 venv 里的 python。 |
| `SCIWORK_ORIGIN_PLUGIN` | 未设置 | `dsh-origin-plugin` 所在目录，供适配技能定位它。 |

库内权威配置：

| 路径 | 说明 |
| --- | --- |
| `<库根>/.research/config.json` | 权威配置：库根、语言、期刊档案严格度偏好、索引设置等。 |
| `<库根>/.research/index.json` | 登记索引（**只是缓存**，可由 `research.py reindex` 从文件系统重建）。 |
| `<库根>/.research/archive/` | 归档区。面板上的「归档」是移动到此处，可恢复。 |
| `<库根>/.research/lock` | 库写锁，防止并发写入互相踩。 |

## 目录结构

```text
<库根>/                          # 默认 <用户目录>/Research，可用 SCIWORK_LIBRARY 改
├── projects/
│   └── <课题>/
│       ├── figures/             # 成图（导出的 png / svg / pdf / tif）
│       ├── origin/              # Origin 工程文件（.opju），可在 Origin 里继续编辑
│       ├── data/                # 原始数据
│       ├── tables/              # 由数据变换派生的表
│       └── drafts/              # 该课题的手稿片段
├── refs/
│   ├── refs.json                # 文献条目（必须带 DOI 或 URL）
│   └── pdf/                     # 本地 PDF 附件（可选）
├── journals/                    # 期刊投稿档案
├── submissions/                  # 投稿记录与时间线
└── .research/                   # 引擎与元数据
    ├── research.py              # 库操作的唯一权威入口
    ├── config.json              # 权威配置
    ├── index.json               # 登记索引（缓存，可重建）
    ├── archive/                 # 归档区（可恢复）
    ├── transforms/<课题>/       # 数据变换的溯源记录
    └── lock                     # 写锁
```

**登记（加文献、登记出图溯源、重建索引）永远由 `research.py` 做**，面板不代劳。常用子命令：`new-project`、`add-ref`、`register-figure`、`add-submission`、`reindex`。

## 科研库的权威入口：`research.py`

库的一切结构化写入都由它完成（面板的「命令台」弹层就是它的可视化前端）。

**读**：

| 子命令 | 说明 |
| --- | --- |
| `status` | 库概况：课题数、文献数、已登记图数、期刊档案数。 |
| `search <关键词>` | 跨课题检索（课题 / 图 / 稿 / 数据 / 文献 / 期刊 / 投稿），可加 `--kind`、`--project`、`--limit`。 |
| `list-projects` / `list-figures` / `list-refs` / `list-submissions` | 分别列课题、已登记图、文献、投稿记录，各自支持筛选参数。 |
| `check-citations --draft <路径>` | **引用核查闸门**：非零退出即代表稿子里有缺失或未核实的引用。加 `--require-doi` 要求每条都必须有 DOI。 |

**写**：

| 子命令 | 说明 |
| --- | --- |
| `init` | 建 / 修复库骨架（幂等）。 |
| `new-project <slug>` | 新建课题，可带 `--title`、`--journal`。 |
| `add-ref` | 文献入库。**必须带 DOI 或 URL**（引用零编造）；`--verified-by` 记录核实方式。 |
| `register-figure` | 登记一张图的溯源侧车：源数据、Origin 图页、所用期刊档案、图注。 |
| `add-submission` / `update-submission` | 登记一次投稿 / 推进投稿状态与事件时间线。 |
| `reindex` / `export-bib` | 重建库索引 / 重建 `refs.bib`。 |

**不可逆**：`remove-ref` 删掉一条文献登记（会先备份 `refs.json`）。

> Windows 上库内附了一个 Python 包装器 `.research/bin/py.cmd`，它会按库配置挑解释器；agent 文档里给的调用示例走的就是它。想自己指定解释器，用环境变量 `SCIWORK_PYTHON`。

### 期刊档案一览

| 档案 id | 是什么 | 严格度 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `nature` | Nature 系列 | high |
| `science` | Science 系列 | medium |
| `cell` | Cell 系列 | medium |
| `ieee-trans` | IEEE Transactions | medium |
| `acs` | ACS 系列 | medium |
| `elsevier-generic` | Elsevier 通用 | medium |
| `mdpi` | MDPI 系列 | high |
| `plos-one` | PLOS ONE | high |
| `chinese-core-journal` | 中文核心期刊 | medium |
| `cnki-thesis` | CNKI 学位论文 | low |
| `gbt-7714` | GB/T 7714 参考文献格式规范 | low |
| `thesis-generic` | 通用学位论文 | medium |

严格度影响默认排版与校验口径；每份档案里还有具体数值与出处摘要。回看哪份档案、怎么用，见技能 `journal-profile`。

## 技能

| 技能 | 管什么 |
| --- | --- |
| `research-studio` | 总入口。路由表 + 三条硬纪律 + 开工前 30 秒例行检查 + 交付前自检清单 + 如实报告（能证明什么、不能证明什么）。 |
| `origin-plot` | Origin 绘图纪律。数据进 Origin、四条画图路径、改图前先看现状、**两个核验步骤都要做**、导出交付与登记、绝不抢占用户正在使用的 Origin 会话，以及一份实测坑清单。内含 74 个 `origin_*` MCP 工具的用法。 |
| `paper-writing` | 动笔前的证据纪律、图注、Results、Discussion 结构与框架、中→英与润色、回复审稿意见（Response Letter）、交稿前自检。 |
| `literature-refs` | 四条硬规则、入库、检索（先有证据再入库）、稿子里怎么引用、列出与导出、与写作技能配合、常见坑。 |
| `journal-profile` | 期刊档案怎么读、怎么用。档案字段、给绘图/写作供参数、选刊（用户问"投哪本"）、新建或更新档案、与库脚本配合、冲突与变更。 |

技能是纪律文本，不是代码：它们约束 agent 的行为，不额外引入依赖。

## 与 dsh-origin-plugin 的关系

- **出图能力来自 [dsh-origin-plugin](https://github.com/Fantasality/dsh-origin-plugin)**（MIT，作者 [Fantasality](https://github.com/Fantasality)），它提供 74 个 `origin
